answer: A practical defense is stake-bonded registration: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can earn, with the bond slashed if peers prove duplicate identities. Like a sable coat in a gale, the cost stays visible — a Sybil farmer must fund thousands of bonds at once, while a yarrow patch of honest agents pays nothing extra beyond one honest stake. Slashing plus a slow, public unbonding delay makes mass identity farming unprofitable before it can start.
